title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
name: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
name: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.
steps:
1. Name Fear — Picture the feared ending in one line.
2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now.

title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
name: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
steps:
1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.

title: THE BLAME PIE
name: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

ritualText:
THE BLAME PIE

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

GOAL
Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.

1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

WIN
✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.

• Give self-compassion enough time to change the next moment.
• Choose growth first, then decide what self-blame needs.
• Choose self-compassion before deciding what self-blame means.
• Give self-compassion more authority than self-punishment.
• Guilt does not cancel your access to self-respect.

FORMULA FLOW
Imagine A Pie → Share The Slices → Check The Whole → Find Your Slice → Choose Repair

PAUSE
Set it down if sharing turns into punishment or erases genuine accountability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: One fact can support more than one world.
steps:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

ritualText:
MOOD HAS ALIBIS

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Test what the day does to the feeling.

1. Choose Activity — Choose one activity.
2. Score Expected — Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add Sentence — Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Try Three Ways — Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’

WIN
✓ The feeling kept its voice but lost the judge’s chair.

• Protect perspective by making the next decision smaller.
• Emotional weather is real; emotional obedience is still optional.
• Use a wider view to make the next hour kinder.
• Keep a calmer check available; emotional weather may not stay this loud.
• Keep balance protected while an intense emotion finds its level.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Activity → Score Expected → Add Sentence → Try Three Ways

PAUSE
Seek professional support if low mood is severe, persistent, or linked to self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

ritualText:
WORD MELT

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

WIN
✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.

• Let more control guide the response, even with automatic behaviour present.
• Autopilot can change shape when pressure drops.
• Do not confuse automatic behaviour with a permanent verdict.
• You can honour automatic behaviour and still refuse autopilot.
• Take autopilot seriously without treating it as destiny.

name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.

title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
name: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
steps:
1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.

title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
steps:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Run Order — Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

ritualText:
PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

GOAL
A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.

1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Run Order — Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

WIN
✓ The body surge lost some of its authority.

• Let present-moment facts reduce the pressure that panic creates.
• Give a surge of fear its real size, not its emotional size.
• Choose safety cues over the short relief of panic fighting.
• Choose what supports more control, not what feeds escape rushing.
• You can honour a racing sensation and still refuse escape rushing.

Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control

Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.

ritualText:
DROP THE APPEAL

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Reality has already entered the room; the appeal is only in your mind.

1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove Approval — Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.

WIN
✓ I stopped appealing reality and moved inside the version that exists.

• Choose a respectful boundary even if conflict heat has not disappeared.
• Let communication strain be one experience, not your whole identity.
• Defensiveness is real; peak-heat speaking is still optional.
• One pause can protect less damage from motive guessing.
• Keep clarity steady while defensiveness moves through.

FORMULA FLOW
State Fact → Remove Approval → Add Nothing

PAUSE
Acceptance must never be used to legitimise abuse, injustice, or preventable harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

ritualText:
PUT GOOD ON THE CALENDAR

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.

1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one really reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect Appointment — Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Lock It In — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’

WIN
✓ Good got a place on the calendar without needing a score.

• Your choice around an intense emotion can be simple: a grounded choice.
• Let emotional weather pass through without turning into mood evidence.
• Choose one verified fact before deciding what a strong feeling means.
• Make space for perspective before asking for certainty.
• Do not use peak-intensity deciding as proof that an intense emotion is correct.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Genuinely → Protect Appointment → Details → Lock It In

PAUSE
Do not force pleasure during grief or depression; attendance itself can be the result.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
name: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.
steps:
1. Identify Chapter — Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling.
2. Permit — Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
3. Pause Meaning — If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet.
4. Continue Genuine — Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears.

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
A feared scene needs a container, not a flood.

1. Set Boundaries — Decide a manageable start, endpoint, grounding phrase, and recovery plan.
2. Recount — Recount or visualise the feared scene slowly without changing key facts.
3. Track Shift — Notice how prediction or emotion changes across the telling.
4. Finish Here — End by naming your present place, date, and one current safety fact.

WIN
✓ Replay closed in the present: current place, current date, current choice.

• Name what is physically present; drifting thoughts do not own the room.
• The present can hold you even while your mind feels far away.
• Give one present detail more authority than story chasing.
• Keep presence in sight when feeling far away narrows attention.
• Let orientation guide you when story chasing starts sounding convincing.

FORMULA FLOW
Set Time → Recount → Prediction → Finish Location

PAUSE
Do not self-administer for severe trauma, psychosis, acute crisis, or destabilising memories.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
name: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
goal: Stay long enough to learn what happens after the peak.
steps:
1. Highest — During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Leave After Recovery — Departure follows learning, not panic.

3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.

ritualText:
REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
A crutch can hide the safety already holding you.

1. Identify Protective — During a manageable practice round, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying extra certainty.
2. Drop Legitimate — Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.

WIN
✓ Pressure separated from importance.

• Keep a sense of progress visible when starting pressure gets loud.
• Keep a sense of progress protected while the delay finds its level.
• Removing one crutch can reveal strength that avoidance kept hidden.
• Let a tiny start reduce the pressure that the stuck feeling creates.
• Do not use overplanning as proof that the delay is correct.

FORMULA FLOW
Identify Protective → Drop Legitimate → Observe Outcome

PAUSE
Never remove medically required or genuinely protective behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

ritualText:
COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.

1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending.

WIN
✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.

• One moment of a short delay can protect more freedom.
• An impulse becomes safer when you stop treating speed as permission.
• Keep craving escalation from turning a craving into a bigger problem.
• Give a deliberate response more authority than impulse obedience.
• Choose more options first, then decide what the urge needs.

FORMULA FLOW
Small → Let Unfold → Stop Completion → Observe Whether

PAUSE
Never direct movement toward a person or continue if aggression escalates.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE FLOOR
name: BORROW THE FLOOR
goal: Let external support do part of the holding.
steps:

title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
name: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
steps:
1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
name: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
steps:

4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

name: FIND THE BUSY HALF
goal: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.
steps:

5. Check Whether — Check if urgency changes when imbalance decreases.

about 1 minute

GOAL
Walking can become a moving attention track.

ritualText:
NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Release both hands of mental grasping.

1. Check The Pull — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

WIN
✓ Rejection became an event, not an identity.

• Keep belonging protected while rejection pain finds its level.
• Use a fairer comparison to stay connected with belonging.
• Use your actual values to make comparison more manageable.
• Ask whether outside measurement helps belonging or only reduces discomfort.
• Pause outside measurement; give your own measure a fair chance.

FORMULA FLOW
Check The Pull → Relax → Let Content → Act According

PAUSE
Do not release practical action needed to protect health, rights, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
goal: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
steps:
1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
steps:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.

title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
name: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
goal: One exception is enough to weaken inevitability.
steps:
1. Name Pattern — Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find Misses — Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare Conditions — Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Transplant Edge — Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.

ritualText:
THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.

1. Open Possibilities — Generate five options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
2. Vary Them — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one unusual safe option.
3. Delay Judgement — Only after all five exist may feasibility enter the room.

WIN
✓ I let options multiply before judgement was allowed into the room.

• Before reacting to the familiar loop, ask what protects choice.
• Do not turn autopilot into a reason for habit obedience.
• Choose what supports a new pathway, not what feeds cue chasing.
• Use one deliberate pause to make automatic behaviour more manageable.
• Choose one conscious choice before deciding that the familiar loop will last.

FORMULA FLOW
Start Brief → Include Conventional → Test Feasibility

PAUSE
Exclude choices that violate ethics, consent, law, or safety from the start.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
name: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
goal: Another lap costs minutes of your actual life.
steps:
1. Name Lap — Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.

goal: One perspective is data, not the whole room.

3. Watch Behaviour — Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
4. Ask Future — Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.

plain:

Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
name: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
steps:
1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS

goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
steps:

ritualText:
LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Analysis may keep interrupting an unfinished inner sequence.

1. Bring Image — Bring up the image gently and prohibit verbal commentary.
2. Allow Move — Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
3. Check Your Position — Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes.
4. Use Sensory — Reorient afterward using present sensory facts.

WIN
✓ I let the image reach its last frame instead of interrupting it with analysis.

• Use the room around you to stay connected with connection.
• Stay close to connection when story chasing feels tempting.
• One dose of one present detail can reopen orientation.
• Your choice around a floating mind can be simple: one present detail.
• Keep present avoidance from turning a floating mind into a bigger problem.

FORMULA FLOW
Bring Image → Allow Move → Check Your Position → Use Sensory

PAUSE
Do not use alone with traumatic imagery, hallucinations, or destabilisation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

goal: Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
name: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
steps:
1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.

title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
steps:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

ritualText:
THE FEELING UNDER THE FEELING ABOUT IT

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Secondary emotion may be wearing the crown.

1. Name Emotion — Spot the primary emotion and its trigger.
2. Finish About — Then finish: ‘About feeling this, I feel…’ Locate each in a different body area or colour.
3. State Needs — Offer the primary state what it needs before addressing shame, anger, or fear about having it.

WIN
✓ The first feeling finally got care before the second one took over.

• Two feelings can coexist without either one becoming the whole truth.
• Keep responsibility proportionate when emotional weather gets personal.
• One moment of a grounded choice can protect more better judgement.
• Choose what supports better judgement, not what feeds emotional obedience.
• When an intense emotion rises, return to a grounded choice.

Name Emotion → Finish About → State Needs

PAUSE
Seek help if peeling exposes overwhelming trauma or self-attack.

title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
name: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
steps:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
name: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.
steps:
1. Seat Feelings — Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Put it into simple words a child could understand.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.

ritualText:
EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

GOAL
Ongoing sense can be sensed before the life story is consulted.

1. Don't Recall — For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
2. Stay Changing — Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Simple — Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
4. End Reclaim — Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.

WIN
✓ For one minute, existence did not need a biography.

• You are more than the story your mind repeats about you.
• Take new evidence seriously when rigid certainty feels overwhelming.
• Choose new evidence before deciding that rigid certainty will last.
• Choose one fresh question before deciding that an old label will last.
• A fixed story can be present while freedom stays possible.

FORMULA FLOW
Don't Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim

PAUSE
Stop if life-story quiet creates feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

ritualText:
ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

GOAL
The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.

1. Headline Event — State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay.
2. Extract Claim — Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route Bill — Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Act Present — Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.

WIN
✓ The old bill met today’s receipt—and stopped charging the present.

• Let forward movement remain possible even if rumination stays.

title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
name: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
goal: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.
steps:
1. Number Doors — Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let Chance Choose — Let the first number that pops into your mind choose the section. Do not pick again just because you dislike it.
3. Enter There — Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Mark Progress — Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.

ritualText:

about 1 minute

GOAL
Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.

WIN

title: LET ONE TASTE FINISH

title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
name: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
steps:
1. Imagine Four Things — Picture four ordinary things from a familiar room.
2. Name Jobs — Give each only its basic job: support, light, hold, open.
3. Drop Demands — Say NOT NEEDED NOW to every function irrelevant to this moment.
4. Choose Helper — Keep only the imagined function that supports your next safe action.

goal: See what the options look like before their names start campaigning.

title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
steps:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
name: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
steps:
1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING

goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.
steps:

4. Let Relationship — Let seeing or hearing itself become primary for several seconds.

title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
steps:

4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps:

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.
steps:
1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS

goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
steps:

4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.
steps:

title: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
name: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
goal: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.
steps:
1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

ritualText:
GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Shrink the Rule — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

WIN
✓ The belief got a postcode instead of a passport to everywhere.

• Choose what supports self-respect, not what feeds rescuing.
• One dose of a respectful no can reopen space.
• External pressure can be loud while your values stay steady.
• Self-respect sometimes means refusing duties that were never truly yours.
• Let self-respect be the measure, not rescuing.

FORMULA FLOW
Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Shrink the Rule
